narrative.overview:
lanlord is a split-flap departures board for one LAN segment. The page is an enamel panel, near-black at night and cool pale enamel in daylight, ruled by hairlines and carrying exactly one signal colour. The register is a timetable: each row opens with when the device was last seen, names the device in sentence case, and closes with a state flap. Nothing is rounded, nothing floats, and nothing is decorated that is not a fact from the last scan.

The system is built for the operator's brief visit, so hierarchy is temporal before it is alphabetical. Present devices stack at NOW, departures keep their place below a structural rule, and the stopwatch at top right states how often the board refreshes. A device that arrived in the last 24 hours carries a 1px amber arrival flag; that and the refresh clock are the only places amber is allowed. The result should feel like infrastructure that was installed, not a dashboard that was assembled.
keyCharacteristics: Enamel ground, ivory flap cells, one amber signal.
Zero radii; 1px rules do all the separating.
Last-seen time leads every row; state closes it.
Split-flap cells for presence, never coloured dots.
Identical light and dark boards, chosen by the system appearance.

rules.name: The Two-Use Amber Rule
rules.body: Amber belongs to the refresh clock and the arrival signal. Focus outlines may borrow it as an accessibility state; nothing else may. Its rarity is how the operator finds "new" in one pass.

rules.name: The Enamel-Not-Cream Rule
rules.body: Daylight ground is cool pale enamel (#eceef0), never warm beige. Warmth lives in the flap cells, not the field.

rules.name: The Sentence-Case Data Rule
rules.body: Device names are data and stay in sentence case. Uppercase is a structural voice for labels, figures, flaps and the wordmark only.

rules.name: The Terse Age Rule
rules.body: Last seen reads NOW, 10 M, 2 H, 21 D. A present device never reads "0 minutes ago".

dos: Do lead every register row with its last-seen age and close it with a state flap.
Do keep the departed group on the page under a structural divider; an empty slice explains itself and links back to the full register.
Do keep amber to the refresh clock and arrival signal; use focus amber only for keyboard state.
Do use tabular numerals for every time, count and address.
Do hold the 11px floor for functional labels and the 4.5:1 contrast floor in both appearances.
Do treat daylight as an equal board: cool enamel ground, inverted flap cells, same amber signal.
donts: Don't round corners, add shadows, or float panels on the board.
Don't use cards, coloured status dots, or a separate "departed" page.
Don't uppercase device names; they are data, not labels.
Don't render a zero-duration age as "0 minutes ago"; use NOW.
Don't add a kicker or eyebrow above a heading, or any ornamental label that does not state a scan fact.
Don't load external fonts, icons or CDN assets; HTMX is vendored and the type is on the machine.
